title: Reconstruct CLIP
summary: Build the dual-encoder alignment objective from normalized embeddings through symmetric contrastive cross-entropy.

parts.title: Natural language supervision
parts.prompt: Why can image-caption pairs provide broader supervision than a fixed class label set?
parts.answer: Captions describe open-ended objects, attributes, and relationships. Training on them avoids committing to one closed ontology and transfers through text prompts at evaluation time.
hints: Compare a caption with a one-hot class.

parts.title: Why normalize embeddings?
parts.prompt: What does L2 normalization change about image-text similarity?
parts.answer: After normalization, dot products equal cosine similarity, so scores reflect direction rather than vector magnitude. This prevents either encoder from winning by increasing norms.

parts.title: Symmetric contrastive learning
parts.prompt: Why compute both image-to-text and text-to-image cross-entropy?
parts.answer: Each direction treats one modality as queries and the other as candidates. Averaging both ensures every image selects its caption and every caption selects its image within the batch.
hints: The similarity matrix can be read by rows or columns.
Matched pairs lie on the diagonal.

parts.title: Implement L2 normalization
parts.prompt: Normalize vectors along their final dimension with numerical protection.

parts.title: Implement CLIP contrastive loss
parts.prompt: Normalize both modalities, form temperature-scaled similarities, and average row-wise and column-wise cross-entropy.
